scr_close_financial_close_management.purpose: The RealPage application that turns month-end and year-end close into a managed workflow: tasks assigned to preparers, balance-sheet work papers compiled automatically from the ledger into an Excel package, and a reviewer/approver sign-off chain per property and period.
scr_close_financial_close_management.outcome: Each property's close becomes a trackable, evidenced process — who did what, by when, and who signed off — rather than a folder of spreadsheets and emails.
scr_close_financial_close_management.rootCause: Institutional multifamily portfolios close hundreds of entities every month, often with an offshore team preparing and an onshore team reviewing across time zones. Without a system of record for the close, deadlines slip invisibly, work papers are inconsistent between properties, and auditors cannot see evidence that reconciliations were reviewed.
scr_close_financial_close_management.ifSkipped: Close status lives in email and personal trackers, owner packages go out without evidence of review, late properties are discovered only when the asset manager complains, and SOC 1 / audit control testing fails for lack of documentation.
gaap: SOC 1 Type II — outsourced accounting control evidence
redFlags: Properties enabled in RealPage accounting but not in Financial Close Management (no close evidence)
Work papers approved by the preparer
Close tasks tracked outside the tool for some properties

scr_close_getting_started.purpose: Orientation for first-time setup of Financial Close Management: logging in, enabling the properties that should produce work papers, granting roles, and building the first work-paper configuration and task list before any close can run through the tool.
scr_close_getting_started.outcome: A correctly scoped close environment where every property in the portfolio is enabled and every accountant has the access needed to prepare, review or approve.
scr_close_getting_started.rootCause: The close tool only works for properties and users that have been explicitly configured. Missed setup is the most common reason a property has no work papers at month-end — typically a newly acquired property onboarded into accounting but never added to close management.
scr_close_getting_started.ifSkipped: New acquisitions close without work papers, users cannot see their tasks, and the first month in the tool produces incomplete packages that reviewers reject.
redFlags: Acquisitions added to the GL but not enabled here
Setup done by one person with no documented configuration

scr_close_roles_and_permissions.purpose: Defines which Financial Close features each user can access — preparing work papers, reviewing, approving, configuring tasks, running close reports — through Company > Setup > Users/Roles.
scr_close_roles_and_permissions.outcome: Enforced segregation of duties: preparers cannot approve their own work, and only designated managers can change close configuration or reopen books.
scr_close_roles_and_permissions.rootCause: Close sign-off is only a control if the approver is independent of the preparer. Owners and auditors test that permissions actually enforce this, especially where offshore staff prepare and onshore staff approve.
scr_close_roles_and_permissions.ifSkipped: Preparers can approve their own packages, junior staff can reopen closed periods, and auditors conclude the review control is not effective.
redFlags: Offshore preparers holding approver rights on their own properties
Terminated users still holding close roles
Too many users with rights to open closed books

scr_close_accessing_the_financial_close_.purpose: The navigation path from the Financial Suite home page into Financial Close Management, where users land on the workflow-style home page for their close responsibilities.
scr_close_accessing_the_financial_close_.outcome: Users reach their close tasks and work papers from a consistent entry point.
scr_close_accessing_the_financial_close_.rootCause: New offshore staff and rotating reviewers need to find the close application quickly. Access also confirms the user's license and role are set up — if the application is missing from the menu, the user was never provisioned.
scr_close_accessing_the_financial_close_.ifSkipped: New team members lose time at month-end hunting for the application or discover on business day 3 that they were never given access.
redFlags: Users who should have access but do not see the application at close start

scr_close_financial_close_management_hom.purpose: Landing page that lays out the close in workflow order — setup, checklists, workbench tasks, work paper generation, review/approval, reports — so users can see where each step of the month-end sits.
scr_close_financial_close_management_hom.outcome: Users understand the close sequence and jump directly to the step they own.
scr_close_financial_close_management_hom.rootCause: Close tools fail when users do steps out of order (generating final work papers before tasks are done). Presenting the workflow visually reinforces the sequence the controller expects.
scr_close_financial_close_management_hom.ifSkipped: Steps are done out of order, causing regenerated packages and repeated reviews.
redFlags: Final packages generated before workbench tasks are complete

scr_close_configuration.purpose: Setup area controlling which properties participate in Financial Close Management and which users are unrestricted (can see all properties regardless of property-level security).
scr_close_configuration.outcome: A defined scope of properties and a controlled list of users with portfolio-wide close visibility.
scr_close_configuration.rootCause: RealPage security restricts users to specific properties. Close managers and reviewers need portfolio-wide visibility, while properties must be explicitly enabled to generate work papers. Configuration keeps both deliberate.
scr_close_configuration.ifSkipped: Some properties never appear in close reports, and reviewers cannot see all the work they must approve.
gaap: COSO 2013 — scope completeness of reconciliation controls
redFlags: Enabled property count differs from the active property count in the GL
Unrestricted access granted broadly

scr_close_configuration_page.purpose: The page, restricted to Limited or Full administrators, where unrestricted users are added and properties are enabled for work papers and close reports, with changes recorded in an audit trail.
scr_close_configuration_page.outcome: Administrator-controlled changes to close scope with a record of who changed what.
scr_close_configuration_page.rootCause: Changing close scope affects whether reconciliations are performed at all. Limiting it to administrators and logging changes prevents someone from quietly removing a problem property from the close.
scr_close_configuration_page.ifSkipped: Properties can drop out of the close unnoticed, and there is no evidence of who changed scope.
redFlags: Properties disabled mid-year without documentation

scr_close_adding_unrestricted_users.purpose: Grants selected users visibility of every enabled property in Financial Close Management — typically onshore reviewers, close managers and team leads who oversee the whole portfolio.
scr_close_adding_unrestricted_users.outcome: Reviewers and managers can monitor and approve work for all properties without being assigned property by property.
scr_close_adding_unrestricted_users.rootCause: Property-level security is right for preparers but blocks oversight roles. Unrestricted access solves this but is powerful, so it must be granted deliberately.
scr_close_adding_unrestricted_users.ifSkipped: Reviewers miss properties they are responsible for; alternatively, if granted too broadly, preparers see and act on properties outside their assignment.
redFlags: Offshore preparers granted unrestricted access without need
No periodic review of the unrestricted list

scr_close_enabling_properties.purpose: Adds properties to Financial Close Management so their ledgers feed work papers and close reports, typically done at onboarding of a new acquisition or management take-over.
scr_close_enabling_properties.outcome: Newly onboarded properties produce work papers from their first close under management.
scr_close_enabling_properties.rootCause: Portfolios change constantly through acquisitions, dispositions and management take-overs. A property that is not enabled simply does not appear in the close, which is easy to miss in a large portfolio.
scr_close_enabling_properties.ifSkipped: New properties close without reconciliations for months, typically discovered at the first audit or owner complaint.
redFlags: Properties sold but still enabled (noise)
Properties acquired but not enabled

scr_close_work_paper_configuration_list_.purpose: Lists all work paper configurations — the templates that define which balance-sheet reconciliations (cash, A/R, A/P, deposits, prepaids, accruals, escrow) are compiled for which properties and on what frequency.
scr_close_work_paper_configuration_list_.outcome: A managed set of package templates, e.g. a standard monthly multifamily package and a quarterly or year-end package, applied consistently across properties.
scr_close_work_paper_configuration_list_.rootCause: Different owners and property types need different reconciliations (commercial properties need CAM reconciliations; agency-financed properties need reserve escrows). Configurations make the package consistent within each group while allowing differences between groups.
scr_close_work_paper_configuration_list_.ifSkipped: Each preparer assembles work papers differently, reviewers cannot compare properties, and required reconciliations are left out.
redFlags: Configurations missing accounts that carry balances
Multiple overlapping configurations for the same property

scr_close_previewing_a_work_paper_config.purpose: Shows what a work paper configuration will produce — which work papers and reports for which properties — before it is used to generate a package.
scr_close_previewing_a_work_paper_config.outcome: Configuration errors (missing properties, wrong reports) are caught before a package is generated at month-end.
scr_close_previewing_a_work_paper_config.rootCause: Generating packages across many properties takes time; discovering the configuration was wrong after generation means regenerating under deadline pressure.
scr_close_previewing_a_work_paper_config.ifSkipped: Packages are generated with missing work papers and must be regenerated, delaying review.
redFlags: Configurations edited without preview before month-end

scr_close_adding_a_new_work_paper_config.purpose: Creates a new work paper configuration — name, frequency (monthly, quarterly, year-end), properties or property groups, and which work papers and reports to include — as the prerequisite for generating any package.
scr_close_adding_a_new_work_paper_config.outcome: A new close package template ready for use, for example when onboarding a new owner with specific reconciliation requirements.
scr_close_adding_a_new_work_paper_config.rootCause: New owners often specify their own reconciliation requirements in the management agreement (e.g., a monthly escrow roll-forward or intercompany schedule). A new configuration encodes those requirements once.
scr_close_adding_a_new_work_paper_config.ifSkipped: The new owner's required reconciliations are not produced, breaching reporting requirements.
redFlags: Configurations created without confirming owner requirements

scr_close_editing_a_work_paper_configura.purpose: Changes an existing work paper configuration — adding properties, adding or removing work papers, changing frequency — when the portfolio or owner requirements change.
scr_close_editing_a_work_paper_configura.outcome: Close packages stay aligned with the current portfolio and reporting requirements.
scr_close_editing_a_work_paper_configura.rootCause: Portfolios change monthly. Configurations that are not maintained produce packages that include sold properties or omit new ones and new reconciliation requirements.
scr_close_editing_a_work_paper_configura.ifSkipped: Packages drift out of date, generating noise or missing work papers.
redFlags: Work papers removed from a configuration mid-year without documented reason

scr_close_duplicating_a_work_paper_confi.purpose: Creates a new work paper configuration by copying an existing one, used for example to build a year-end configuration from the monthly one with additional reports added.
scr_close_duplicating_a_work_paper_confi.outcome: Faster, consistent setup of related configurations without rebuilding them from scratch.
scr_close_duplicating_a_work_paper_confi.rootCause: Year-end and quarterly packages usually extend the monthly package. Copying preserves the standard monthly content and reduces setup errors.
scr_close_duplicating_a_work_paper_confi.ifSkipped: Year-end configurations are built from scratch and miss standard monthly work papers.
redFlags: Duplicated configurations left pointing to the original properties when they should differ

scr_close_tasks_list_page.purpose: Maintains the library of close tasks — e.g., post GPR entry, post depreciation, reconcile operating bank, amortize prepaids, accrue utilities, review variance notes — that are later assembled into checklists and assigned to preparers.
scr_close_tasks_list_page.outcome: A standardized task catalog that defines what 'closing a property' means for the organization.
scr_close_tasks_list_page.rootCause: A consistent close depends on the same tasks being done for every property every month. The task library is where the controller defines those tasks once.
scr_close_tasks_list_page.ifSkipped: Checklists are built ad hoc, tasks are missed, and close quality varies by preparer.
redFlags: Tasks without instructions or owner
Obsolete tasks still active

scr_close_viewing_a_task.purpose: Opens a close task definition to see its description, instructions, assignment and settings, and to print, duplicate or edit it.
scr_close_viewing_a_task.outcome: Preparers and reviewers can confirm exactly what a task requires before completing or signing off.
scr_close_viewing_a_task.rootCause: Offshore preparers need clear written instructions for each task; reviewers need to confirm the task was done as defined.
scr_close_viewing_a_task.ifSkipped: Tasks are interpreted differently by different preparers.
redFlags: Task instructions out of date with current process

scr_close_adding_a_task.purpose: Creates a new close task in the library — for example 'Record servicer escrow disbursements' or 'Tie rent roll to GPR' — with its description and settings, so it can be included in checklists.
scr_close_adding_a_task.outcome: New close requirements (new owner request, audit finding, new process) become a trackable task.
scr_close_adding_a_task.rootCause: Audit findings and owner requests regularly add close steps. Unless they become tasks, they depend on memory and are forgotten.
scr_close_adding_a_task.ifSkipped: Remediation of audit findings is not embedded in the close, and the same finding recurs.
redFlags: Audit findings without a corresponding close task

scr_close_editing_a_task.purpose: Modifies a close task's description, instructions or settings when the process changes (new report, new threshold, new reviewer).
scr_close_editing_a_task.outcome: Task definitions stay aligned with current procedures.
scr_close_editing_a_task.rootCause: Processes evolve; outdated task instructions lead preparers to follow superseded procedures.
scr_close_editing_a_task.ifSkipped: Preparers follow outdated steps and reviewers reject work.
redFlags: Task edits without communicating changes to preparers

scr_close_duplicating_a_task.purpose: Copies an existing close task to create a similar one — for example duplicating 'Reconcile operating bank' to create 'Reconcile security deposit trust bank'.
scr_close_duplicating_a_task.outcome: Related tasks are created quickly with consistent instructions.
scr_close_duplicating_a_task.rootCause: Many close tasks are variations of each other (one per bank account type or escrow type). Duplicating keeps instructions consistent.
scr_close_duplicating_a_task.ifSkipped: Similar tasks are written inconsistently, confusing preparers.
redFlags: Duplicated tasks left with the original task's wording

scr_close_close_checklist_page.purpose: Assigns the monthly close tasks to accountants by entity or location and tracks completion through month-end, forming the day-by-day close calendar (e.g., cash recs by BD3, accruals by BD4, package by BD7).
scr_close_close_checklist_page.outcome: A visible, assigned close calendar per property that shows who owns each task and what is late.
scr_close_close_checklist_page.rootCause: Close deadlines are tight and involve many handoffs between offshore preparers and onshore reviewers. An assigned checklist makes ownership and deadlines explicit.
scr_close_close_checklist_page.ifSkipped: Tasks fall between team members, deadlines are missed, and nobody knows which properties are behind.
redFlags: Tasks assigned to users who are out of office
Tasks without due dates

scr_close_viewing_the_close_checklist.purpose: Reviews a close checklist's tasks, assignees, due dates and status, with export to CSV, Excel, PDF or Word.
scr_close_viewing_the_close_checklist.outcome: Managers can monitor progress and share status with clients.
scr_close_viewing_the_close_checklist.rootCause: Close status must be reviewed daily during close and communicated to onshore managers and clients.
scr_close_viewing_the_close_checklist.ifSkipped: Late tasks are discovered too late to recover.
redFlags: Tasks marked complete without evidence

scr_close_adding_a_close_checklist.purpose: Creates a new close checklist for a period and set of entities, pulling tasks from the task library and assigning preparers, reviewers and due dates.
scr_close_adding_a_close_checklist.outcome: A ready-to-run checklist for the month's close.
scr_close_adding_a_close_checklist.rootCause: Each period needs its own checklist to record completion. Creating it before month-end gives preparers their assignments before the close begins.
scr_close_adding_a_close_checklist.ifSkipped: The close starts without assignments and tasks are claimed ad hoc.
redFlags: Checklist created after the close has already started

scr_close_select_tasks_box.purpose: Search box used while building or editing a checklist to find tasks in the library and add them.
scr_close_select_tasks_box.outcome: The checklist includes every required task from the standard library.
scr_close_select_tasks_box.rootCause: Large task libraries make it easy to miss tasks; a searchable selector helps ensure completeness.
scr_close_select_tasks_box.ifSkipped: Required tasks are omitted from the checklist.
redFlags: Checklists missing standard tasks such as bank reconciliation

scr_close_editing_a_close_checklist.purpose: Modifies an existing checklist — reassigning tasks when staff are absent, changing due dates, adding tasks for a one-off event such as a refinancing or property sale.
scr_close_editing_a_close_checklist.outcome: The checklist reflects actual staffing and period-specific requirements.
scr_close_editing_a_close_checklist.rootCause: Close conditions change mid-month (staff absence, special transactions). Updating the checklist keeps ownership accurate.
scr_close_editing_a_close_checklist.ifSkipped: Tasks remain assigned to unavailable staff, and one-off requirements are missed.
redFlags: Due dates extended repeatedly for the same tasks

scr_close_deleting_a_close_checklist.purpose: Removes a close checklist, typically one created in error or for the wrong period or entities.
scr_close_deleting_a_close_checklist.outcome: Duplicate or erroneous checklists are removed so status reporting is accurate.
scr_close_deleting_a_close_checklist.rootCause: Duplicate checklists confuse status and can show tasks as incomplete when they were completed elsewhere.
scr_close_deleting_a_close_checklist.ifSkipped: Status reports show duplicates and false incomplete tasks.
gaap: Record retention — do not delete checklists that evidence completed controls
redFlags: Deleting checklists with completed tasks (loss of evidence)

scr_close_exporting_close_checklist_resu.purpose: Exports the close checklist with task status, assignees and completion dates to a file for evidence, client reporting or SLA analysis.
scr_close_exporting_close_checklist_resu.outcome: A retained record of close completion for the period.
scr_close_exporting_close_checklist_resu.rootCause: Auditors and clients need evidence of close completion in a retainable format outside RealPage.
scr_close_exporting_close_checklist_resu.ifSkipped: No durable evidence of close performance for the period.
redFlags: Exports not retained with close files

scr_close_monthly_checklist_page.purpose: Assigns tasks that must be completed during the month — not only at month-end — such as weekly deposit reviews, bi-weekly payment runs, lender reporting due mid-month and quarterly compliance items.
scr_close_monthly_checklist_page.outcome: Recurring intra-month responsibilities are tracked alongside the month-end close.
scr_close_monthly_checklist_page.rootCause: Much property accounting work happens throughout the month. Tracking only month-end tasks leaves intra-month obligations (lender reports, sales tax filings) unmonitored.
scr_close_monthly_checklist_page.ifSkipped: Intra-month deadlines (lender reports, tax filings) are missed.
redFlags: Lender reporting deadlines not in the monthly checklist
